reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about the role of a chromium-rich oxide layer in corrosion resistance, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge may cover the general role of passive films, but the specific claims about layer thickness, uniformity, and stability under varying conditions require supporting citations, which are absent.
premises: Corrosion resistance is governed by a chromium-rich oxide layer
The oxide layer acts as a barrier to chloride ion penetration
Thicker, more uniform oxide layers provide higher corrosion resistance
Layer stability is compromised at higher temperatures and chloride concentrations
Cathodic protection can be used to control the oxide layer's effect
